Listen to this article Share Eleven years after it began as a design studio in Akure, Nigerian design consultancy FourthCanvas is entering the United Kingdom market, where it plans to work with startups and established businesses seeking support with their brands. The consultancy, now headquartered in Lagos, said it had registered a UK business and secured its first fintech client in the country. Tunji Ogunoye, who joined the team in 2016 and previously served as Director of Design, has now been appointed Country Director for the UK operation. His immediate task is to build local relationships and adapt the company’s approach to a different business environment. For Victor Fatanmi, co-founder and Director of Strategy the decision follows years of preparation. “After 11 years, we’ve learnt enough to begin to substantiate what had always been a global ambition. Our system has matured, our work has matured,” he said. The company sees opportunities among Nigerian entrepreneurs establishing businesses in the UK, as well as local firms. Its work will cover brand positioning, design and communication. The consultancy said the increasing migration of Africans to the UK and other international markets was reshaping how brands engaged with multicultural audiences. It noted that broad demographic segmentation could overlook the distinct consumer behaviours, cultural perspectives and expectations within African communities. Businesses seeking to reach diaspora communities or expand across borders therefore needed a more specific understanding of those audiences, the company said. It added that its experience building brands in African markets, combined with local UK insight, would inform its approach to these relationships. Ogunoye said the consultancy’s experience with startups had exposed it to the changing needs of businesses as they grow. Beyond creating a visual identity, he said, the work involves helping a company explain what it does, where it belongs in the market and why customers or investors should pay attention. He acknowledged, however, that experience gained in Nigeria would have to be applied with an understanding of the UK market. “Context differs. Way of doing things differs,” Ogunoye said. Understanding the cultural environment, including how people make business decisions, would be part of that process, he added. Founded in 2015, FourthCanvas has built an 11-year design practice spanning brand strategy, identity, communication and activations for startups and established organisations. According to the consultancy, its work has included assignments for ALX, M-KOPA, TLCOM, Notto, Piggyvest, Raenest, The Stack Group (Paystack), Nigerian Breweries, Titan Trust Bank and ThriveAgric. The consultancy also reports serving clients in Kenya and South Africa. The UK operation marks its first formal overseas establishment, extending a practice already serving businesses across African markets. Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha is the Aviation Correspondent at BusinessDay Media Limited, publishers of BusinessDay Newspapers. She is also the Deputy Editor, BusinessDay Weekender Magazine, the Saturday Weekend edition of BusinessDay. She holds a BSC in Mass Communication from the prestigious University of Nigeria, Nsukka and a Masters degree in Marketing at the University of Lagos. As the lead writer on the aviation desk, Ifeoma is responsible and in charge of the three weekly aviation and travel pages in BusinessDay and BDSunday. She also overseas and edits all pages of BusinessDay Saturday Weekender. She has written various investigative, features and news stories in aviation and business related issues and has been severally nominated for award in the category of Aviation Writer of the Year by the Nigeria Media Nite-Out awards; one of the Nigeria’s most prestigious media awards ceremonies. Ifeoma is a one-time winner of the prestigious Nigeria Media Merit Award under the 'Aviation Writer of the Year' Category. She is the 2025 Eloy Award winner under the Print Media Journalist category. She has undergone several journalism trainings by various prestigious organisations. Ifeoma is also a fellow of the Female Reporters Leadership Fellowship of the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism.
